title: How should AI agents hand work back to people?
dek: The best agent teams are not the ones that do everything. They are the ones that know exactly when to stop and ask.
summary: AI agents should hand work back at the moment an action becomes hard to undo: a send, a deploy, a payment. A good handoff arrives as a finished draft with its evidence attached, so a person can approve it in one read.

hero.alt: The Verifier Momo, cut from blue and kraft paper, studying a tag through a magnifying glass

body.heading: When should an agent stop and ask?
paragraphs: Whenever the next step leaves the building. Research, drafting and checking are cheap to redo; an email sent or a budget spent is not.
Drawing that line once, in writing, saves a hundred judgment calls later.

body.heading: What makes a good handoff?
paragraphs: A finished draft, not a question. The evidence it relied on, linked. A one line statement of what happens if the person says yes.

body.heading: Does this slow the work down?
paragraphs: Less than it seems. The agent does the long part; the person spends a minute on the part that carries the risk. That is the trade clients are paying for.
